what: HER2, also called ERBB2, is a gene.
The public summary in this snapshot says extra HER2 is found in 20 to 30 percent of invasive breast cancers.
intro.test_report: If a test report mentions HER2, it is noting a finding about this gene. That note is not a diagnosis, and it is not a decision about treatment.

lines.text: Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine (KADCYLA): a lab-made antibody linked to a drug. Approved for breast cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2013.
Fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan (ENHERTU): a lab-made antibody linked to a drug. Approved for breast cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2020.
Lapatinib: a pill. Approved for breast cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2008.
Margetuximab (MARGENZA): a drug that blocks the HER2 signal. Approved for breast cancer with HER2-positive disease.
Neratinib (Nerlynx): a drug that blocks the HER2 signal. Approved for breast cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2018.
Pembrolizumab (KEYTRUDA QLEX): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for stomach cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2015.
Pertuzumab (Perjeta): a drug that blocks the HER2 signal. Approved for breast cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2013.
Sevabertinib (HYRNUO): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for advanced lung cancer.
Tislelizumab (TEVIMBRA): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for stomach cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2023.
Trastuzumab (Herceptin): a drug that blocks the HER2 signal. Approved for breast cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2000.
Tucatinib (TUKYSA): a drug that blocks the HER2 signal. Approved for breast cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2020.
Zanidatamab (ZIIHERA): a lab-made antibody. Approved for stomach cancer with HER2-positive disease. Authorised in Europe since 2025.
Zongertinib (HERNEXEOS): a drug named on the FDA label in this snapshot. Approved for advanced lung cancer.
